summary: Smith County tower that the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists as gone; no source found describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what remains at the site.

evidence.supports: Starrville is in northern Smith County, three miles east of Winona and about a mile northeast of Starrville Mountain
evidence.quote: Starrville is three miles east of Winona and one mile northeast of Starrville Mountain at the intersection of Farm roads 757 and 16 in northern Smith County

evidence.supports: In 1852 a Methodist minister, Joshua Starr, bought the 640-acre Hall Survey and began offering town lots for sale
evidence.quote: In 1852 the Reverend Joshua Starr, a Methodist minister from Alabama, bought the Hall Survey, all 640 acres, and began selling town lots

evidence.supports: The post office name was changed to Starrville in 1857
evidence.quote: The name of the post office was changed to Starrville in 1857

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Only the FFLA list (Gone, coordinates), a 2011 list tagged TFS (the page names a Texas Forest Service list of 91 towers among its sources), and the Handbook of Texas were found. An earlier draft said the page does not explain the TFS tag; the page does explain it, so the story was corrected. No build date, agency, staffing, photo or removal date found. The Handbook places the town about a mile northeast of a landmark called Starrville Mountain. A GNIS peak named Starrville Mountain in data/sources/peaks_gnis.json sits roughly 200 m from the record point, but no source ties the tower to it, so the story does not. Story is about 120 words, at the 120-word target, with the evidence this thin.
